description: We’re a team of one. so I covered every role myself: product idea, game design, testing and quality checking, and project documentation and worked with an AI assistant (Claude) to code, while I directed each change and tested every result. My main strength on this project was persistence: I found the bugs, spotted the balance problems and kept iterating until the game worked.
summary: A playable, deterministic simulation of a four-person Moon or Mars outpost in which you keep the crew alive through real solar storms, and learn why radiation, power and supplies trade off against each other
details:
Outpost Twin is a playable digital twin of a four-person Moon or Mars outpost. You manage power, air, water, food and cabin heat one hour at a time, and you can copy the live mission and run it forward to test a plan before committing. Each mission replays a real stretch of space weather: when a solar particle event from NASA’s DONKI archive arrives, you choose to shelter (almost no dose, but no outdoor work and a cramped crew) or carry on (people outside take the full dose). Doses add up toward NASA’s 600 mSv career limit. Passing it grounds a person and slowly costs health, and a big dose in one storm makes someone ill.

The aim is to show that radiation is a budget, not a single event. In my scripted tests over a busy 365-day year, a crew that always carries on lost everyone, while a crew that sheltered from strong storms and watched its dose survived.

Two modes run the same rules: Assisted (plain words, hints, fewer controls) and Standard (every control). Everything is labelled “Real world” with a source link or “Game rule” when it is my estimate. Storm timing, surface dose rates and the limits are real. Storm doses and penalties are game estimates, because the archive gives no dose.

Built with JavaScript modules, Vite and three.js. It includes a self-test that runs 560 scripted missions and checks the numbers stay sane. I’m a solo participant: I designed, playtested and balanced the game, and used an AI assistant (Claude by Anthropic) to help write the code.
